companyDescription: Space Infrastructure · Lunar landers + cislunar communications + national security space — transitioning from moon-lander story to space-to-Earth communications platform with $1.1B backlog
priceNote: Consolidating at $21-22 after analyst upgrades — 52-week range wide, Clear Street upgraded to top pick for 2026
summary: Intuitive Machines delivered record Q1 2026 revenue of $186.7M (up ~3x YoY) with $1.1B backlog — a $842M increase driven by Lanteris acquisition and new CLPS task orders. 2026 revenue guidance is $900M–$1B with positive adjusted EBITDA. With analyst consensus at $40.78 (+88% upside), Roth Capital at $50, and Clear Street calling LUNR its top pick for 2026, the space infrastructure thesis is compelling. Strategic acquisitions of Goonhilly + COMSAT add 44 antennas and deep-space ground assets, transforming LUNR into a cislunar communication platform.

catalysts.name: Golden Dome — National Security Space Contracts
catalysts.description: LUNR secured a contract under Andromeda IDIQ with US Space Force, ceiling value $6.24B. Golden Dome initiative driving multi-year national security space infrastructure demand. NASA + DoD backlog at $1.1B.

catalysts.name: Goonhilly + COMSAT Acquisitions
catalysts.description: Acquisitions of Goonhilly Earth Station (UK) and COMSAT add 44 antennas and deep-space communications assets in U.S. and UK — transforms LUNR into space-to-Earth communications platform beyond just lunar landers.

catalysts.name: NASA Lunar Terrain Vehicle + CLPS Missions
catalysts.description: NASA Lunar Terrain Vehicle contract and additional CLPS task orders moving through procurement. 60-65% of $1.1B backlog converting to 2026 revenue = $660M–$715M floor revenue.

risks: EPS miss on Q1 2026 — LUNR missed EPS consensus (net loss $0.25 vs consensus -$0.06) despite record revenue; profitability path uncertain
Mission execution risk — lunar landing failures (IM-1 tipped over on landing) create contract risk and public perception issues
Government contract timing uncertainty — NASA + DoD procurement cycles can shift revenue recognition quarters
High valuation for pre-profit company — any revenue guidance reduction triggers sharp derating

estimateDates.note: Andromeda IDIQ ceiling $6.24B — any task order = catalyst

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Government space contracts are multi-year, funded by congressional appropriations — largely independent of Fed rate cycles
macroRisk.inflationNote: Space infrastructure costs are largely labor and specialized hardware — moderate inflation exposure. National security funding is inflation-protected.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Space sector re-rating underway as Golden Dome, Artemis, and commercial space commerce expand. LUNR is direct beneficiary of US government space infrastructure push.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk LOW — LUNR revenue is government-contract-driven (NASA + DoD + Space Force). Appropriations-funded contracts are rate-insensitive. Main risks are mission execution and EPS trajectory, not macro.

postWin.note: LUNR +35% in 1 week when Lanteris acquisition + $429M new awards announced (Q1 2026). Pattern: contract win + backlog growth = sharp re-rating. Clear Street upgraded to $44 after Q1 results drove +18% same day.

postLose.note: IM-1 lunar lander tipped over on landing (Feb 2024) dropped -35% as mission partial failure. Mission execution risk is the key bear case for LUNR.

spotSizing.reason: Speculative 74/100 — $1.1B backlog gives confidence but EPS losses and mission risk limit sizing. Max 6% of portfolio. Scale in on dips.
